prompt:
Build a task-scheduling pipeline in four new modules of the more_itertools package. Each stage consumes the previous stage's output, so build them in order and keep the data shapes below exactly.

Order matters: requirement N imports and builds on requirement N-1.
1. more_itertools/lg_dag_build.py: build(text) returns a dict node -> sorted list of its successors from lines 'a->b' (whitespace around names ignored, blank lines skipped, duplicate edges collapsed). A line 'a' alone declares a node with no edges. Every node mentioned appears as a key. A line with an empty name or more than one '->' raises ValueError.
2. more_itertools/lg_dag_topo.py: topo_order(graph) takes the dict from lg_dag_build.build and returns a deterministic topological order (Kahn's algorithm, always taking the lexicographically smallest ready node). A cycle raises ValueError('cycle').
3. more_itertools/lg_dag_sched.py: schedule(graph, durations) returns a dict node -> earliest start time, where a node starts when all its predecessors have finished (start of a predecessor plus its duration); durations is a dict node -> number and a missing node counts as 1. Uses lg_dag_topo.topo_order (import it); a cycle propagates its ValueError.
4. more_itertools/lg_dag_crit.py: critical_path(text, durations) builds the graph from the text with lg_dag_build, schedules it with lg_dag_sched (import both), and returns (length, path): length is the latest finish time (start plus duration, missing duration 1), path is the list of nodes of one longest chain from first to last, ties broken toward the lexicographically smallest node names. Empty graph gives (0, []). Cycles propagate ValueError.

All functions are plain Python with no third-party dependencies. Do not modify existing modules or tests.
Commit your work on a new branch and push it.
